In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Rather, you do not honour the orphan, and you do not urge one another to feed the poor﴾ [al-Fajr 89:17-18]. That means the needy person who has nothing to sustain himself and meet his needs.

Then He said: ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and others said: It means the hypocrites, who pray openly but do not pray in private.

For this reason He said: ﴿to those who pray﴾, that is, those who belong to the people of prayer and have committed themselves to it, yet they are heedless of it. This heedlessness may be: (1) from performing it at all, as Ibn 'Abbas said; or (2) from performing it within the time specified for it by the Law, so that they take it outside its time entirely, as Masruq and Abu al-Duha said; or (3) from performing it at its first time, so that they delay it to its very end, always or usually; or (4) from performing it with its pillars (arkan) and conditions (shurut) in the manner commanded; or (5) from humility (khushu') in it and reflection upon its meanings. As is established in the two Sahihs, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "That is the prayer of the hypocrite, that is the prayer of the hypocrite, that is the prayer of the hypocrite: he sits watching the sun until, when it is between the two horns of the Shaytan, he stands and pecks four times, not remembering Allah in it except a little." Then he stood up for it and pecked it like a crow, not remaining still in it and not being humble in it either. For this reason he said: "He does not remember Allah in it except a little." Perhaps what moved him to stand for it was showing off to people (riya' al-nas), not seeking the Face of Allah, and so he had not prayed at all. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them. And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people, and they do not remember Allah except a little﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:142]. Here He said: ﴿those who show off﴾.

Al-Tabarani said: Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abdawayh [In M, A: "'Abd Rabbih"] al-Baghdadi narrated to us, my father narrated to me, 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed in Jahannam there is a valley (lawadiyan) [In M, A: "li-wad"] from which Jahannam seeks refuge every day four hundred times. [al-Musnad 2/212.]

Abu Ya'la al-Hafiz narrated it likewise from Shayban ibn Farrukh, from 'Ikrimah ibn Ibrahim, with the same chain. [Musnad Abi Ya'la 2/63.] This has the stronger chain (asahh isnadan). As for His saying ﴿and they withhold al-Ma'un﴾: that means they did not do good in worshipping their Lord, nor did they do good to His creation, not even by lending what is beneficial and used for help while its substance remains and it returns to them. So those who withhold zakat and the various kinds of acts of devotion are even more deserving of this description. Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid that 'Ali said: al-Ma'un is zakat. Likewise al-Suddi narrated it from Abu Salih, from 'Ali. It was also narrated from more than one route from Ibn 'Umar. Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, 'Ata', 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, al-Zuhri, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd also said this.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: If he prays, he shows off; and if he misses it, he does not regret it; and he withholds the zakat of his wealth. In another wording: "the charity of his wealth."

Zayd ibn Aslam said: They are the hypocrites: the prayer appeared, so they prayed it; and the zakat was guaranteed, so they withheld it.

Al-A'mash and Shu'bah narrated from al-Hakam, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, that Abu al-'Ubaydayn asked 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud about al-Ma'un, and he said: It is what people lend to one another of the axe, the cooking pot, [and the bucket] [addition from M, A]. [And al-Mas'udi narrated from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-'Ubaydayn: that Ibn Mas'ud was asked about al-Ma'un, and he said: It is what people exchange among themselves, of the axe, the cooking pot, the bucket, and similar things] [addition from M, A].

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to me, Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-'Ubaydayn and Sa'd ibn 'Iyad, from 'Abd Allah who said: We, the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, used to say that al-Ma'un is the bucket, the axe and the cooking pot, which one cannot do without.

Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, Shu'bah informed us, from Abu Ishaq who said: I heard Sa'd ibn 'Iyad narrate from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ the like of this. [Tafsir al-Tabari 30/205.]

Al-A'mash said, from Ibrahim, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, from 'Abd Allah, that he was asked about al-Ma'un, and he said: What people lend to one another: the axe, the bucket and the like.

Ibn Jarir said: 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas narrated to us, Abu Dawud [that is, al-Tayalisi] narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abd Allah who said: We were with our Prophet ﷺ, and we used to say: al-Ma'un is withholding the bucket and similar things. [Tafsir al-Tabari 30/206.]

The wording of al-Nasa'i from 'Abd Allah is: "Every ma'ruf (good deed) is charity, and we used to count al-Ma'un in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as the lending of the bucket and the cooking pot."

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and they withhold al-Ma'un﴾, meaning: the household goods (mata' al-bayt). Likewise Mujahid, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Malik and others besides them said: it is lending of household items.

Layth ibn Abi Sulaym said, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and they withhold al-Ma'un﴾. He said: "Its people have not yet come [after them]."

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And withhold common kindnesses﴾ that he said: "People differed about this. Some said: they withhold zakat. Some said: they withhold obedience. Some said: they withhold lending (al-'ariyyah)." Ibn Jarir related it.

Then it was narrated from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn 'Ulayyah, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from 'Ali: "al-Ma'un (common kindnesses) is people withholding the axe, the cooking pot, and the bucket."

'Ikrimah said: "The head of al-ma'un is zakat on wealth, and its lowest level is the sieve, the bucket, and the needle." Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

What 'Ikrimah said is good, for it encompasses all the sayings, and they all return to one thing, which is refraining from helping others with wealth or benefit. For this reason Muhammad ibn Ka'b said regarding ﴿And withhold common kindnesses﴾: "It is al-ma'ruf (what is good and known)." For this reason there came in the hadith: "Every act of ma'ruf is a charity."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, Waki' related to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Zuhri regarding ﴿And withhold common kindnesses﴾: "In the language of Quraysh, it means property (al-mal)."

He also related here a hadith that is strange and wondrous in both its chain and its text, saying:

My father and Abu Zur'ah related to us, both saying: Qays ibn Hafs al-Darimi related to us, Dulhum ibn Dahtham al-'Ijli related to us, 'A'idh ibn Rabi'ah al-Numayri related to us, Qurrah ibn Du'mus al-Numayri related to me: that they came as a delegation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you enjoin upon us?" He said: "Do not withhold al-ma'un." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-ma'un?" He said: "In the stone, in the iron, and in the water." They said: "Which iron?" He said: "Your copper cooking pots, and the iron of the axe with which you are occupied." They said: "And what is the stone?" He said: "Your stone cooking pots."

[[Ibn Mardawayh also related it, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (644).]]

It is extremely strange; its raising to the Prophet (ﷺ) is munkar (rejected), and in its chain is someone who is not known. And Allah knows best.

Ibn al-Athir mentioned in the section on the Companions the biography of "'Ali al-Numayri," and said: Ibn Qani' related with his chain to 'A'idh ibn Rabi'ah ibn Qays al-Numayri, from 'Ali ibn Fulan al-Numayri: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim. When he meets him, he greets him with peace, and returns to him what is better than it, and does not withhold al-ma'un.'" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-ma'un?" He said: "The stone, the iron, and the like."

[[Usd al-Ghabah (3/624).]]

End of the tafsir of Surat al-Ma'un.

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Rather, you do not honour the orphan, and you do not urge one another to feed the poor﴾ [al-Fajr 89:17-18]. That means the needy person who has nothing to sustain himself and meet his needs.

So those who withhold zakat and the various kinds of acts of devotion are even more deserving of this description. Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid that 'Ali said: al-Ma'un is zakat. Likewise al-Suddi narrated it from Abu Salih, from 'Ali. It was also narrated from more than one route from Ibn 'Umar. Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, 'Ata', 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, al-Zuhri, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd also said this.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: If he prays, he shows off; and if he misses it, he does not regret it; and he withholds the zakat of his wealth. In another wording: "the charity of his wealth."

Zayd ibn Aslam said: They are the hypocrites: the prayer appeared, so they prayed it; and the zakat was guaranteed, so they withheld it.

Al-A'mash and Shu'bah narrated from al-Hakam, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, that Abu al-'Ubaydayn asked 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud about al-Ma'un, and he said: It is what people lend to one another of the axe, the cooking pot, [and the bucket] [addition from M, A]. [And al-Mas'udi narrated from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-'Ubaydayn: that Ibn Mas'ud was asked about al-Ma'un, and he said: It is what people exchange among themselves, of the axe, the cooking pot, the bucket, and similar things] [addition from M, A].

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to me, Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-'Ubaydayn and Sa'd ibn 'Iyad, from 'Abd Allah who said: We, the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, used to say that al-Ma'un is the bucket, the axe and the cooking pot, which one cannot do without.

Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, Shu'bah informed us, from Abu Ishaq who said: I heard Sa'd ibn 'Iyad narrate from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ the like of this. [Tafsir al-Tabari 30/205.]

Al-A'mash said, from Ibrahim, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, from 'Abd Allah, that he was asked about al-Ma'un, and he said: What people lend to one another: the axe, the bucket and the like.

Ibn Jarir said: 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas narrated to us, Abu Dawud [that is, al-Tayalisi] narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abd Allah who said: We were with our Prophet ﷺ, and we used to say: al-Ma'un is withholding the bucket and similar things. [Tafsir al-Tabari 30/206.]

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated it from Qutaybah, from Abu 'Awanah with his chain, similarly [Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1657; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 11701]. The wording of al-Nasa'i from 'Abd Allah is: "Every ma'ruf (good deed) is charity, and we used to count al-Ma'un in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as the lending of the bucket and the cooking pot."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah who said: al-Ma'un: the 'awari (loaned goods): the cooking pot, the scales, and the bucket.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and they withhold al-Ma'un﴾, meaning: the household goods (mata' al-bayt). Likewise Mujahid, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Malik and others besides them said: it is lending of household items.

Layth ibn Abi Sulaym said, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and they withhold al-Ma'un﴾. He said: "Its people have not yet come [after them]."

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And withhold common kindnesses﴾ that he said: "People differed about this. Some said: they withhold zakat. Some said: they withhold obedience. Some said: they withhold lending (al-'ariyyah)." Ibn Jarir related it.

Then it was narrated from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn 'Ulayyah, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from 'Ali: "al-Ma'un (common kindnesses) is people withholding the axe, the cooking pot, and the bucket."

'Ikrimah said: "The head of al-ma'un is zakat on wealth, and its lowest level is the sieve, the bucket, and the needle." Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

What 'Ikrimah said is good, for it encompasses all the sayings, and they all return to one thing, which is refraining from helping others with wealth or benefit. For this reason Muhammad ibn Ka'b said regarding ﴿And withhold common kindnesses﴾: "It is al-ma'ruf (what is good and known)." For this reason there came in the hadith: "Every act of ma'ruf is a charity."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, Waki' related to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Zuhri regarding ﴿And withhold common kindnesses﴾: "In the language of Quraysh, it means property (al-mal)."

He also related here a hadith that is strange and wondrous in both its chain and its text, saying:

My father and Abu Zur'ah related to us, both saying: Qays ibn Hafs al-Darimi related to us, Dulhum ibn Dahtham al-'Ijli related to us, 'A'idh ibn Rabi'ah al-Numayri related to us, Qurrah ibn Du'mus al-Numayri related to me: that they came as a delegation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you enjoin upon us?" He said: "Do not withhold al-ma'un." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-ma'un?" He said: "In the stone, in the iron, and in the water." They said: "Which iron?" He said: "Your copper cooking pots, and the iron of the axe with which you are occupied." They said: "And what is the stone?" He said: "Your stone cooking pots."

[[Ibn Mardawayh also related it, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (644).]]

It is extremely strange; its raising to the Prophet (ﷺ) is munkar (rejected), and in its chain is someone who is not known. And Allah knows best.

Ibn al-Athir mentioned in the section on the Companions the biography of "'Ali al-Numayri," and said: Ibn Qani' related with his chain to 'A'idh ibn Rabi'ah ibn Qays al-Numayri, from 'Ali ibn Fulan al-Numayri: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim. When he meets him, he greets him with peace, and returns to him what is better than it, and does not withhold al-ma'un.'" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-ma'un?" He said: "The stone, the iron, and the like."

[[Usd al-Ghabah (3/624).]]

End of the tafsir of Surat al-Ma'un.
